question: What will be the amount to be paid at the end of 5 years on Rs. 4500 at 10% per annum compounded annually?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective compound interest rate for 10% per annum over 5 years can be directly derived from the multiplying factor 1.1

We know that 1.1⁵ = 1.61051, meaning the total amount becomes 161.051% of the principal.

Amount = 1.61051 × 4500

⇒ Amount = 7247.295

⇒ Rounding to one decimal place, we get 7247.3

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7247.3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4500

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% per annum

Time (n) = 5 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
•

 Each step × 1.1 (+10%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 4500 × (1 + 10/100)⁵

⇒ A = 4500 × (11/10)⁵

⇒ A = 4500 × 1.61051

⇒ A = 7247.295

⇒ Amount ≈ ₹7247.3

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7247.3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Compound Interest Rates

For a 10% interest rate, the effective CI is 21% for 2 years, 33.1% for 3 years, and 46.41% for 4 years. Remembering these saves significant calculation time in exams.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on the same principal is computed as Diff = P × (R/100)².

Rule of 72

The approximate time required to double your principal amount at a given compound interest rate can be found directly using 72 ÷ R.
